sections.title: Base System Conversions and Arithmetic in Different Bases
sections.content: To convert a decimal number N into base b: (1) Repeatedly divide N by b. (2) Record each remainder. (3) Stop when quotient becomes zero. (4) Read remainders in reverse order. (5) Verify that each digit is less than b. (6) Reconvert to decimal to confirm accuracy. For number of digits of N in base b: compute floor(log N / log b) + 1. For addition or multiplication in base b: align digits, apply carry whenever sum or product reaches b, and reduce using base rules.

sections.title: Advanced Applications of Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT)
sections.content: For simultaneous congruences N ≡ a (mod m) and N ≡ b (mod n), where m and n are co-prime: (1) Express N = m*k + a. (2) Substitute into second congruence. (3) Solve resulting congruence in k modulo n. (4) Determine k using modular inverse if required. (5) Substitute back to obtain N. (6) Express final solution modulo m*n. For three or more congruences, solve pairwise and reduce step by step.

sections.title: Writing a Number as Product of Two Co-Primes
sections.content: If N = p^a × q^b × r^c, the number of ways to express N as product of two co-prime integers equals (a+1)(b+1)(c+1). Steps: (1) Prime factorize N. (2) For each prime, decide how its entire power is assigned to either factor. (3) Ensure no prime is shared between factors. (4) Multiply independent choices. (5) If order does not matter, adjust for symmetry.

sections.title: Sum, Product, and Reciprocal Sum of Factors
sections.content: If N = p^a × q^b, then total number of factors d = (a+1)(b+1). Sum of factors equals [(p^(a+1)-1)/(p-1)] × [(q^(b+1)-1)/(q-1)]. Product of all factors equals N^(d/2). Sum of reciprocals of factors equals (sum of factors) divided by N. Steps: (1) Factorize N. (2) Compute d. (3) Apply geometric series formula. (4) Compute product formula. (5) Divide by N for reciprocal sum.

sections.title: Advanced Factorial Manipulations
sections.content: To divide n! by a composite number M: (1) Prime factorize M. (2) Compute exponent of each prime in n! using floor division method. (3) Compare required exponents with available exponents. (4) Determine how many times M divides n!. (5) Simplify remaining factorial expression if required. (6) Verify divisibility conditions.

sections.title: Number System Integrated with Permutations and Combinations
sections.content: To form numbers satisfying divisibility conditions: (1) Identify total permutations of given digits. (2) Apply divisibility rules (such as last digit, sum of digits, or last two digits conditions). (3) Fix constrained positions first. (4) Count remaining arrangements. (5) Subtract invalid cases if needed. (6) Present final count after simplification.

integrated_models.title: Base Conversion Combined with Modular Logic
integrated_models.description: Convert expression into suitable base to simplify structure, then apply modular arithmetic or CRT to determine remainder or digit pattern.
integrated_models.steps: Convert base → reduce expression → apply modular theorem → solve congruence → reconstruct final result.

integrated_models.title: Factor Structure Integrated with Factorial Theory
integrated_models.description: Use prime exponent analysis of factorials along with divisor formulas to evaluate large divisor or remainder problems.
integrated_models.steps: Prime factorization → exponent comparison → divisor formula application → logical elimination → final computation.

integrated_models.title: Divisibility-Constrained Number Formation Model
integrated_models.description: Combine combinatorics with number theory rules to count numbers satisfying advanced remainder or divisibility properties.
integrated_models.steps: Total permutations → impose remainder condition → restrict digit placement → eliminate overlaps → compute final value.
